transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point. No — do not use or charge it again, even briefly. A battery that has become hot, swollen and split its casing is damaged and can become a fire risk. The swelling and split case mean this is not something that can be made safe by cleaning contacts or leaving it to cool. Unplug the charger from the mains and disconnect the battery from the vacuum only if it separates normally without force. Keep the battery away from anything flammable, out of direct sun and away from children or pets. Do not squeeze it, tape the seam, dismantle it, put it in a bin, or take it to a normal battery-recycling point in this condition. Contact Shark support or a qualified battery-recycling/hazardous-waste service for their instructions on safe collection or disposal, and have the IZ201UK model details ready. The charger should also be checked before any replacement battery is used; an engineer or Shark support is the appropriate route.

candidates: Failed lithium-ion battery cells or internal battery protection fault (high)

reading.symptom: battery got very hot while charging and is swollen with the case split at the seam

plan: They asked: "Can I still use it until a new one arrives?" - answer that first.

Safety: a battery hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Shark; model IZ201UK.
The fault they reported is: "battery got very hot while charging and is swollen with the case split at the seam". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
